headline: Palantir's technology chief disputes Bloomberg's report that over-reliance on its AI contributed to the US strike on an Iranian school, saying the likely cause was human error.
score_reason: Pool 6 kept: the interview aired on 11 Oct 2026 and the transcript supports the headline; it is one company executive's account against an earlier press report, with no evidence given and no final report yet.
importance_line: The question of who is accountable when AI-assisted targeting goes wrong affects civilians in war zones first, then Congress (120 House Democrats have written to Secretary Hegseth about this case) and the Pentagon, then Palantir and other military AI suppliers, but Sankar speaks for the company named in Bloomberg's report, gave no evidence in the interview and said the Pentagon's final report, which is not public, should be awaited.
summary: CBS News reports that Palantir's chief technology officer Shyam Sankar, asked on "Face the Nation" on 11 Oct 2026 about the US strike on a school in Minab, Iran that host Margaret Brennan said killed at least 123 schoolchildren, called "inaccurate" a Bloomberg report that some staff leaned too heavily on the AI in Palantir's Maven platform, which the US military uses for intelligence and targeting work, saying the "likely cause is human error" but that the Pentagon's final report should be awaited. Bloomberg's investigation of 18 Sep 2026, based on officials who described an unreleased Pentagon review, had named overreliance on Maven alongside bad intelligence and outdated satellite imagery; Sankar did not say which part he disputes, deferred to the Pentagon on when its report will appear, and said Palantir has since added AI agents that double-check more of the work.
notes: Read the full CBS transcript. Reply story: Sankar answers Bloomberg's 18 Sep 2026 report; its date and content come from Gizmodo's 20 Sep 2026 account and the Google News listing, Bloomberg itself was not opened, and the earlier story was not in our recent editions. 'US strike' rests on the Pentagon references in the transcript and on Gizmodo. The 123 figure is the host's. Regional find with pool score 6; the interview (11 Oct 2026) is inside the window, so the score is kept.
